title: T&C compliance: AI disclosure, registration, demo video, eligibility
body:
## Parent
#1

## What to build
Satisfy the Metropolis Hackathon Terms & Conditions (`docs/terms-and-conditions.md`) as
mandatory requirements, not nice-to-haves. Disqualification is the failure mode here. Scope
is deliberately limited to the compliance gates that issue #7 does NOT already cover — #7 owns
README content, demo video script, and the bounty checklist.

## Acceptance criteria

From §4.1.1 — mandatory submission contents:
- [x] Open source license present (MIT, added)
- [ ] README states that AI coding tools were used, naming which (§4.1.4 — mandatory disclosure, currently a disqualification risk)
- [ ] Public repo, commit history spanning the build window (1 Sep–13 Oct 2026)
- [ ] Monad mainnet or testnet deployment evidenced by transaction hashes (§4.1.3, §9.2)

From §4.1.2 and §9.4 — demo video:
- [ ] Recorded, publicly accessible, **≤ 3 minutes hard** (§9.4), showing the product in actual operation including a real Monad transaction (§4.1.2)
- [ ] Demonstrates a *successful* top-up, not the 503 out-of-stock path (#3 blocker)

From §2 and §4.2 — eligibility and registration:
- [ ] Team registered on hackathon.monad.xyz, 1–5 members (§2.4)
- [ ] Primary contact designated as the prize recipient (§2.4, §6.1 — prizes paid to this wallet)
- [ ] Team eligible: 18+, no sanctions-list jurisdiction (§2.1, §2.2)
- [ ] Registered for exactly one track, submitting one project (§2.5 — multiple submissions disqualify)
- [ ] Deadline booked: 13 Oct 2026, 11:59 PM ET, submitted via the website only (§4.2)

## Blocked by
- #3 — the demo video needs a funded relayer to show a real successful payment

## Notes
Prize pool is stated as $145,000 in T&C §3.2 but $250,000+ on the website; §3.2 notes sponsor
bounties are added later. Plan against the T&C figure.

The exact submission checklist on hackathon.monad.xyz is still login-gated and unread — confirm
against it before submitting.
